sport_profiles.planning_summary: Swimming is a technical water sport where safety, breathing, stroke mechanics, water confidence, event specificity, starts/turns/underwaters, pacing, and shoulder/back/knee load management shape the plan.
training_priorities: water confidence and safety before volume
breathing rhythm and floating/gliding for beginners
stroke-specific development for backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, and IM
starts, turns, streamlines, and underwater phases when safe and relevant
event-specific pacing for sprint, middle-distance, distance, open-water, and triathlon
shoulder/scapular, trunk, thoracic, posterior-chain, and ankle/kick support
yardage, intensity, tool, and stroke-specific load monitoring
do_not_pair: high paddle/pull volume with shoulder symptoms
high butterfly volume with low-back or shoulder symptoms
breaststroke kick volume with knee or groin pain
max breath-holding with any fitness prescription
heavy upper-body dryland immediately before key pool quality
progression_guardrails: progress water safety before fitness volume
progress continuous distance before intensity for beginners
progress yardage before adding tools like paddles
use 24-hour shoulder/back/knee/groin response before adding load
match swim sets to event role and stroke ability

sport_training_rules.title: Freestyle front crawl mechanics
sport_training_rules.rule: Freestyle front crawl mechanics
sport_training_rules.summary: Freestyle front crawl mechanics
blocked_action: ['lifting_head_to_breathe', 'crossing_midline', 'dropped_elbow_catch', 'pulling_immediately_after_entry', 'overkicking_endurance_sets', 'holding_breath']

detail.model: Freestyle front crawl mechanics
detail.body_position: Long horizontal line with eyes mostly down/forward-down, stable head, hips near surface, and rotation driven by shoulders/trunk/hips.
detail.catch_pull: Enter in front between head centerline and shoulder line, extend patiently, then set forearm/hand to hold water and press backward through the body line before clean exit.
detail.kick: Small continuous flutter kick from hips with relaxed ankles; use lower kick count for endurance economy and stronger kick support for sprint or race-pace work.
detail.breathing: Exhale in the water, turn with body rotation, keep one goggle or low head position when possible, inhale quickly, and return face before the pulling arm rushes.

progressions_by_level.beginner: Bubble exhale, prone float, streamline glide, kick with board or side support, 6 to 12.5 m freestyle fragments with relaxed side breath.
progressions_by_level.intermediate: 25 to 100 m repeats with stroke count, bilateral or controlled single-side breathing, drill-swim transfers, and pace that preserves body line.
progressions_by_level.advanced: Race-pace stroke-count targets, stroke-rate changes at same line quality, catch-pressure work without shoulder symptoms, and event-specific breath patterns.

sport_training_rules.title: Backstroke mechanics
sport_training_rules.rule: Backstroke mechanics
sport_training_rules.summary: Backstroke mechanics
blocked_action: ['head_lift', 'hips_sinking', 'flat_no_rotation', 'pulling_down_too_soon', 'bicycle_kick', 'poor_wall_awareness']

detail.model: Backstroke mechanics
detail.body_position: Supine horizontal line with ears near the water, eyes up/back, hips close to surface, relaxed neck, and steady rotation around the long axis.
detail.catch_pull: Thumb-led recovery, little-finger entry near shoulder line, patient catch, bent-elbow pull with palm oriented to push water toward feet, and finish near thigh.
detail.kick: Flutter kick from hips with close legs and relaxed ankles; knee bend remains small and does not break the body line excessively.
detail.breathing: Use a consistent inhale/exhale rhythm tied to arm cycles, avoiding breath holding because the face is exposed.

progressions_by_level.beginner: Back float, back glide, supported back kick, 10 to 25 m head-still backstroke with wall awareness.
progressions_by_level.intermediate: 25 to 100 m repeats with rotation, steady breathing, stroke count, and clean lane positioning.
progressions_by_level.advanced: Race-tempo backstroke with stable line, underwater breakout integration, turn approach counts, and speed changes without over-arching.

sport_training_rules.title: Breaststroke mechanics
sport_training_rules.rule: Breaststroke mechanics
sport_training_rules.summary: Breaststroke mechanics
blocked_action: ['knees_too_wide', 'knees_drawn_to_chest', 'head_lift_instead_of_shoulder_rise', 'overwide_arm_pull', 'no_glide', 'scissor_or_asymmetric_kick']

detail.model: Breaststroke mechanics
detail.body_position: Streamlined glide with shoulders, hips, and legs close to horizontal, head aligned during glide, and hips held up as the legs recover.
detail.catch_pull: Hands pitch out from the glide, elbows remain relatively high, hands sweep out then in toward the upper chest, and arms recover forward into a narrow streamline.
detail.kick: Heels recover toward the seat, knees stay controlled and not excessively wide, feet turn out for the propulsive phase, legs sweep back and together into a long line.
detail.breathing: Shoulders lift the face to air during the pull; avoid throwing the head up because it drops hips and increases low-back/neck load.
detail.timing: Pull, breathe, kick, glide. The glide should be long enough to regain line but not so long that speed stalls.

progressions_by_level.beginner: Teach kick shape on deck or wall, then on back or with support; add short glide-kick repeats before full stroke.
progressions_by_level.intermediate: 25 to 50 m repeats emphasizing narrow kick, legal timing, and glide control; monitor knee/groin response.
progressions_by_level.advanced: Race-tempo timing, pullout integration if appropriate, count-plus-split work, and volume caps based on knee/back symptoms.

sport_training_rules.title: Butterfly mechanics
sport_training_rules.rule: Butterfly mechanics
sport_training_rules.summary: Butterfly mechanics
blocked_action: ['muscling_with_arms', 'late_breath', 'head_stays_up', 'single_large_kick', 'hips_drop_during_recovery', 'low_back_whip']

detail.model: Butterfly mechanics
detail.body_position: Crown/head leads a low-surface body wave with shoulders and hips coordinated; avoid excessive vertical lift or lumbar arching.
detail.catch_pull: Hands enter near shoulder width, set into a Y-shaped catch, sweep inward with high elbows, then press back toward the hips before low relaxed recovery.
detail.kick: Two dolphin kicks per arm cycle for most teaching: one supports entry/catch timing and one helps recovery; movement begins from hips with legs close and ankles relaxed.
detail.breathing: Breath should ride the body wave; shoulders lead the head, inhale quickly, and return the head before or with arm entry. Side breathing may be used selectively if it preserves line.

progressions_by_level.beginner: Use body dolphin and short kick skills only; avoid long full-stroke butterfly sets.
progressions_by_level.intermediate: Single-arm and 3-3-3 drill progressions, 6 to 15 m full-stroke fragments, generous rest, and stop when rhythm fails.
progressions_by_level.advanced: Race-quality 12.5 to 50 m repeats, breathing-pattern control, catch pressure, and underwater-to-breakout integration with back and shoulder monitoring.
